_comment: Project-scoped Claude Code config. Loaded by cloud apps (iOS, Mac, web) that can't reach the user's ~/.claude/. Each project hook script begins with a self-skip preamble: if ~/.claude/hooks/<basename> exists (local CLI), the project copy exits 0 and the user-level master fires. On cloud sandboxes ~/.claude/hooks/ does not exist, so the project copy runs. See .claude/CLOUD.md.
_comment_permissions: Server-level MCP allow: 'mcp__<server>' pre-approves ALL tools from that server (per docs.claude.com permissions ref), so cloud sessions can self-schedule PR/CI check-ins (send_later/create_trigger) without an approval wall — no need to enumerate or verify individual tool ids. Cloud sessions name the server 'Claude_Code_Remote' (tools are mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__*), so the old 'claude-code-remote' entry never matched and add_repo/send_later kept hitting the approval wall (BRO-4216); both spellings are listed. Harmless on local CLI where the server isn't connected. KNOWN LIMIT (BRO-4236, confirmed 2026-09-28 — do not re-attempt this fix for these two tools): despite this rule being live since 2026-09-21, mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__add_repo (grants push credentials to a repo) and send_later (creates a self-firing scheduled trigger) still prompt for interactive approval on iOS/cloud sessions. These two are almost certainly host-level always-confirm gates on the Claude Code Remote platform itself, not something client-side permissions.allow can suppress — likely intentional, so no local config can silently grant repo credentials or self-scheduling. If this recurs, don't re-add allow rules; it's a platform behavior, not a settings gap.

hooks.command: G="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; R="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$G}"; H="$R/.claude/hooks/notion-create-block.sh"; if [ -n "$R" ] && [ -f "$H" ]; then exec bash "$H"; else echo "FATAL: cannot resolve hook script $H (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-unset}, PWD=$PWD, git-toplevel=${G:-none})" >&2; exit 2; fi
